authority_table_decision: deliberately NOT re-owned. Ownership would implicitly grant the control plane UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE, ALTER and DROP over append-only scientific lineage, which is exactly what 0011 withheld ('UPDATE/DELETE are withheld and additionally refused by the append-only trigger'). Nothing requires it: a table carries no definer semantics, and the re-owned resolver reads the table through the SELECT grant 0011 already gave minos_admin. minos_admin's grant on it remains exactly [INSERT, SELECT].

checks.mypy: Success: no issues found in 224 source files

downgrade_defect_found_and_fixed: without the re-grant the round trip silently strips minos_admin's EXECUTE: while it owns a function its explicit grant is absorbed into the implicit owner entry, and handing ownership back drops that entry with it. Pinned by a dedicated regression.
downgrade_policy: ALTER FUNCTION ... OWNER TO CURRENT_USER, then re-issue 0011's two EXECUTE grants. No owner is recorded in a table and none is hard-coded; the lifecycle test proves the assumption it rests on, that the principal running these migrations is the principal that owned the 0011 objects at 0016.
fail_closed_conditions: minos_admin is a SUPERUSER (re-owning would fix nothing)
minos_admin has LOGIN (a group role must not become a login definer)
either named signature does not resolve to an existing function

findings.action_taken: reported, not folded in. They are evaluator-facing rather than runner-facing, and this corrective was authorized for the 0011 runner boundary only; widening a privileged change past its authorization is how privileged changes go wrong.
findings.detail: 0009/0010 created evaluation.l2f_record_evaluation_result, evaluation.l2f_record_evaluation_failure, evaluation.l2f_register_metrics_artifact and evaluation.l2f_register_train_truth_identity as SECURITY DEFINER owned by the migration superuser. The tables evaluation.l2f_evaluation_results and evaluation.l2f_evaluation_failures are likewise superuser-owned, unlike every other L2-F table.
findings.remedy_requires_authorization: a migration re-owning those four functions to minos_admin, with the same OID/body/ACL preservation controls and an evaluator-side runtime proof
findings.title: four evaluation-schema SECURITY DEFINER functions have the same defect

function_acl_note: no MINOS role gains or loses EXECUTE. PostgreSQL necessarily rewrites the ACL's GRANTOR when ownership moves — privileges are granted BY the owner — so the stored aclitem strings change form: the superuser's implicit owner entry disappears and minos_admin's explicit grant is absorbed into its own owner entry. Effective grants are asserted unchanged for every MINOS role and PUBLIC.
